name: gopkg.in/yaml.v2
license_evidence: LICENSE (Apache License 2.0) and LICENSE.libyaml (MIT, for the files ported from libyaml) in the pinned Go module zip
input_api: yaml.Unmarshal([]byte, out) over one complete local YAML byte slice; out is a harness type implementing the documented yaml.Unmarshaler hook, which decodes sequences into a slice of itself, mappings into yaml.MapSlice (source order) and scalars into interface{}
documentation_evidence: The v2.4.0 docs document Unmarshal(in []byte, out interface{}), the Unmarshaler interface (UnmarshalYAML(unmarshal func(interface{}) error) error) and MapSlice as an ordered map that preserves key order when decoding.
scope: One local YAML document decoded into Go values and reported as the typed tree of controls/yaml/check_controls.py; yaml.v2 resolves plain scalars with YAML 1.1 rules, so only the schema-neutral control subset is verified
family: go-yaml v2: Go port of libyaml scanner/parser (scannerc.go, parserc.go, readerc.go) with go-yaml resolve.go/decode.go
family_note: The scanner and parser are a Go translation of libyaml (MIT-licensed files), so the lexical family is shared with C libyaml and its bindings, but there is no C code or cgo. yaml.v3 is the successor in the same project; sigs.k8s.io/yaml and ghodss/yaml are wrappers over a go-yaml v2 fork and v2 respectively. The null scalar does not reach UnmarshalYAML in yaml.v2, so the harness reports an untouched element as null.

name: gopkg.in/yaml.v3
license_evidence: LICENSE in the pinned Go module zip: MIT for the files ported from libyaml, Apache License 2.0 for the rest (NOTICE included)
input_api: yaml.Unmarshal([]byte, *yaml.Node) over one complete local YAML byte slice; Node.ShortTag() resolves each scalar and Node.Decode decodes it
documentation_evidence: The v3.0.1 docs document Unmarshal(in []byte, out interface{}), that decoding into a yaml.Node keeps the document representation (Kind, Tag, Value, Content, Alias), Node.ShortTag and Node.Decode.
scope: One local YAML document decoded into a yaml.Node tree and reported as the typed tree of controls/yaml/check_controls.py; aliases are followed through Node.Alias; only the schema-neutral control subset is verified
family: go-yaml v3: Go port of libyaml scanner/parser (scannerc.go, parserc.go, readerc.go) with go-yaml v3 resolve.go/decode.go
family_note: The scanner and parser are a Go translation of libyaml (MIT-licensed files), so the lexical family is shared with C libyaml and its bindings, but there is no C code or cgo. It shares lineage with the selected yaml.v2 path (same project, separate code base per major version); go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 continues it.

name: github.com/goccy/go-yaml
license_evidence: LICENSE (MIT, Copyright (c) 2019 Masaaki Goshima) in the pinned Go module zip
input_api: yaml.UnmarshalWithOptions([]byte, *interface{}, yaml.UseOrderedMap()) over one complete local YAML byte slice; every mapping decodes into yaml.MapSlice in source order, scalars into string, int64/uint64, float64, bool or nil
documentation_evidence: The v1.19.2 docs document UnmarshalWithOptions(data []byte, v interface{}, opts ...DecodeOption), the UseOrderedMap() DecodeOption ("can be interpreted as a map, and returns MapSlice instead of map[string]interface{}") and MapSlice/MapItem as an ordered map.
scope: One local YAML document decoded with UseOrderedMap into Go values and reported as the typed tree of controls/yaml/check_controls.py; go-yaml expands aliases while decoding; only the schema-neutral control subset is verified
family: goccy/go-yaml: independent pure-Go scanner, lexer, parser, AST and decoder (not a libyaml port)
family_note: Written from scratch in Go (scanner/, lexer/, parser/, ast/, decode.go); it imports neither go-yaml nor libyaml. Only 133 of its 5,391 distinct non-test source lines also occur in gopkg.in/yaml.v3 v3.0.1 (134 for yaml.v2 v2.4.0), all trivial lines such as braces and returns. It is the one selected Go YAML path outside the go-yaml/libyaml lineage.

name: go.yaml.in/yaml/v4
license_evidence: LICENSE (Apache License 2.0) and NOTICE in the pinned Go module zip: the files under internal/libyaml ported from libyaml (api, emitter, parser, reader, scanner, writer, yaml, yamlprivate) stay under the MIT license
input_api: yaml.Load([]byte, *yaml.Node) with the default v4 options over one complete local YAML byte slice; Node.ShortTag() resolves each scalar and Node.Load decodes it
documentation_evidence: The v4.0.0 docs document Load(in []byte, out any, opts ...Option), the Node type (Kind, Tag, Value, Content, Alias), Node.ShortTag and Node.Load; the README marks v4.0.0 as the stable release with v2 and v3 frozen.
scope: One local YAML document loaded into a yaml.Node tree with the v4 Load API and reported as the typed tree of controls/yaml/check_controls.py; aliases are followed through Node.Alias; only the schema-neutral control subset is verified
family: go-yaml v4: Go port of libyaml scanner/parser (internal/libyaml scanner.go, parser.go, reader.go) with new v4 composer, resolver and constructor stages
family_note: Same go-yaml project and libyaml-derived lineage as the selected yaml.v2 and yaml.v3 paths, but a new major version with its own code base: 1,649 of its 6,091 distinct non-test library source lines (27%) also occur in gopkg.in/yaml.v3 v3.0.1, which in turn shares 44% of its lines with v4. The scanner and parser were moved to internal/libyaml and the decoder split into composer, resolver and constructor stages. go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 and go.yaml.in/yaml/v2 are renames of the selected v3 and v2 code, not this path.

name: github.com/go-rotini/yaml
license_evidence: LICENSE (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Matt Getz) in the pinned Go module zip
input_api: yaml.UnmarshalWithOptions([]byte, *interface{}, yaml.WithOrderedMap()) over one complete local YAML byte slice; every mapping decodes into yaml.MapSlice in source order, scalars into Go string, integer, float64, bool or nil values
documentation_evidence: The v1.2.6 docs document UnmarshalWithOptions(data []byte, v any, opts ...DecodeOption), the WithOrderedMap() DecodeOption (decoding into any produces MapSlice values for mappings instead of map[string]any, preserving key order) and MapSlice/MapItem{Key, Value}; the package doc describes YAML 1.2.2 encoding and decoding with Core, JSON and Failsafe schema resolution.
scope: One local YAML document decoded with WithOrderedMap into Go values and reported as the typed tree of controls/yaml/check_controls.py; go-rotini/yaml expands aliases while decoding; only the schema-neutral control subset is verified
family: go-rotini/yaml: independent pure-Go YAML 1.2.2 scanner, parser and decoder (not a libyaml port)
family_note: Written in Go in one package (scanner.go, parser.go, decode.go, unmarshal.go); its go.mod has no requirements, so it imports neither go-yaml, goccy/go-yaml nor libyaml. Its option and type names (UnmarshalWithOptions, MapSlice) resemble goccy/go-yaml, but its code does not: of its 4,596 distinct non-test source lines, 199 (4.3%) also occur in goccy/go-yaml v1.19.2, 151 (3.3%) in gopkg.in/yaml.v3 v3.0.1, 136 (3.0%) in gopkg.in/yaml.v2 v2.4.0 and 181 (3.9%) in go.yaml.in/yaml/v4 v4.0.0, all trivial lines such as braces and returns. Very low adoption (2 importing packages); the README names it the default YAML package of the author's rotini CLI framework.

name: github.com/yongjohnlee80/golib/parse/yaml
license_evidence: LICENSE (Apache License 2.0) and NOTICE (Copyright 2026 Yong Sung John Lee) in the pinned Go module zip; the NOTICE puts only bundled Unicode data and the vendored yaml-test-suite test data under other licenses
input_api: pyaml.Parse([]byte) from github.com/yongjohnlee80/golib/parse/yaml over one complete local YAML byte slice (one document required in Stream.Docs), then yaml.Evaluate(doc, yaml.Core) from the same module's github.com/yongjohnlee80/golib/yaml; mappings become yaml.Map (ordered []MapItem{Key, Value}), scalars nil, bool, int64, float64 or string
documentation_evidence: The v0.8.62 docs of parse/yaml document Parse(src []byte, opts ...Option) (*Stream, error), Stream.Docs and the Node tree (a parser that resolves nothing: scalar Value after folding, escapes and chomping; aliases bound to their Target). The golib/yaml docs document Evaluate(doc *pyaml.Document, schema Schema, opts ...Option) (any, error) with the YAML 1.2 Core schema, constructing nil, bool, int64, float64, string, []any and Map (entries in source order).
scope: One local YAML document parsed into the parse/yaml node tree and evaluated under the YAML 1.2 Core schema by the same module's golib/yaml package, reported as the typed tree of controls/yaml/check_controls.py; Evaluate constructs each alias as its anchored value; only the schema-neutral control subset is verified
family: golib parse/yaml: independent pure-Go YAML 1.2 scanner, parser and composer, with the same module's golib/yaml Core-schema evaluator (not a libyaml port)
family_note: The YAML parser of a large utility monorepo (github.com/yongjohnlee80/golib, which also holds SQL, TUI, server and other unrelated packages). parse/yaml (scanner.go, parser.go, compose.go) builds the YAML 1.2 event stream and node tree and resolves no tags; its README reports all 402 tests of the vendored yaml-test-suite (data-2022-01-17) passing. The schema step is the same module's golib/yaml (Imported by 1), which resolves tags under the YAML 1.2 Core schema and constructs Go values; the harness calls both, and coverage and AFL++ feedback cover exactly these two packages. Its non-test imports outside them (golib/errs, highlight, parse, parse/internal/lexical) are error, highlighting and editor helpers that the controls do not execute and that are not instrumented. Of parse/yaml's 1,178 distinct non-test source lines at most 62 (5.3%) also occur in any selected Go YAML module (goccy/go-yaml v1.19.2); of golib/yaml's 353 at most 41 (11.6%, go.yaml.in/yaml/v4), all trivial lines. Very low adoption (2 importing packages for parse/yaml).
